title: Data of the twisted-pullback tower-domain statement
statement: Use the finite-field and coefficient data, strict varying-ring towers, section-preserving realization, smooth morphism f of relative dimension d, given exceptional adjoint G and coefficient unit from [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers], [def-weil-derived-tensor], [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], [det-sp-tower-gluing], [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object], [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels]. Define B=f* K, U=the coefficient unit, omega=G U, P=B tensor the ordered shifted Tate line, Q=B tensor omega, and orientationMap=1 tensor the given orientation. OriginIn at n means a bounded constructible etale origin of that level with the specified Tor interval, with no cross-level compatibility. DiagonalLevels records the published finite diagonal equations. Conclusion is the record of all original tower-domain conclusions: finiteness and Noetherian hypotheses, pullback/Tate-line and P/Q bounds, membership, orientation invertibility, independent origins and ambient lower bounds, and invertibility/membership of the specified projection source and target. These are the original nine definitions, unchanged.
